newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka fx market ends steady on high dlr supply.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka fx market ends steady on high dlr supply.

text.p: The Sri Lanka rupee closed little changed against the dollar on Tuesday amid high dollar supply, dealers said.
The rupee closed at 58.85 to the dollar after opening at 58.84, they said.
"There was moderate demand for dollars. But since the market was well offered, it had hardly any impact on the exchange rate despite the central bank's action," said a foreign bank dealer.
The central bank pushed up the dollar by 2.75 local cents, fixing higher buying and selling rates at 58.8060 and 59.9990 to account for the dollar's rise on world markets.
Dealers expected the dollar-rupee exchange rate to remain at current levels unless an extra-large import bill emerges due to the regular dollar inflows from the stock market.
Overnight call money rates were low, with the market being well offered, dealers said.
"Overnight call money opened at nine percent and rose for a short while to about 10 but closed at nine percent due to the market being well offered," said a Sampath Bank dealer.
